description: The always-on keeper's instance-state decision table: given what gcloud.find_instance reported for the singleton box, decide whether to acquire/start/leave-alone. Extracted from the DNA-Entropy-Genbank prototype (commit 8026bf5c4afbe3021c1f7e79a17a93af4eaad84b) before its cloud/ package was gutted (issue #280/#284). Reproduces dna_entropy.cloud.keeper._next_action(existing: (zone, status) | None) -> (action, zone).
function_signature: _next_action(existing: tuple[str, str] | None) -> tuple[str, str | None]

source.repo: DNA-Entropy-Genbank (local checkout, matches the migration inventory commit exactly)
source.generated_by: worker/scratch_gen_keeper_fixtures.py, run once against that checkout's own .venv, then deleted (not committed -- see issue #213's closing report for the exact command)
source.verified: Every case here was produced by actually CALLING the prototype's real _next_action() (not read off its test file's asserted values), and cross-checked against tests/test_keeper.py::test_next_action's own 7 parametrized cases, which it matches exactly. This is a pure function of two strings with no I/O, no floating point, and no machine-dependent output -- exact-value comparison is safe for every field here, unlike the stdout-bearing fixtures in this same directory.

port_note: This decision table itself is superseded by design D1 ("Per-job VM, found by label, never by fixed name ... no shared singleton") -- there is no single BOX_NAME instance to look up any more, so this exact function has no direct C# port. Recorded because the STATE-CLASSIFICATION logic (which statuses count as up/stopped/transitional) is still the right reference for whatever per-job VM state polling the C# reconciler does (design section 4.4), even though the surrounding acquire/start/leave-alone decision it drove does not carry over.
